To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the semantic category of a target noun influences the speed of the retrieval of an appropriate Dutch adjective and that the grammatical gender of a target noun has the same effect.
(1) speakers retrieve the meaning they want to convey and (2) speakers retrieve syntactically appropriate information to develop a well-formed syntactic frame.
semantic and syntactic information interact in the production of Dutch adjective noun phrases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the semantic and syntactic information that guides speaking is represented and how it is accessed during speaking.
the question how the speaker’s lexicon and the speaker’s syntactic competence are related in language production.
the relationship between retrieving lexical representations that specify the meaning the speaker intends to communicate and retrieving syntactically appropriate representations for that meaning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the semantic and syntactic information in the lexicon are independent, and the syntactic information is used to select the appropriate syntactic frame.
the semantic and syntactic information in noun phrase production is a feedforward flow that is guided by the syntactic information specific for each word.
the syntactic and semantic forces are both present in the production of noun phrases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the semantic and the syntactic information are not independent.
the syntactic frame for the sentence is built up as soon as possible in the production process and is then used to guide the selection of lexical items.
the production of noun phrases involves the retrieval of semantic information and the development of syntactic information in an interdependent manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the retrieval of a lexical representation that corresponds to our intentions and its integration with syntactic information are not two separate processes, but rather two processes that are closely linked.
semantic and syntactic information interact during the production of noun phrases, and that this interaction can be observed at the level of individual words.
the retrieval of lexical items that specify the meaning of an intended utterance is not an isolated process.
